item.title: Artemis Switch: following a frame from the network to the screen
item.description:
antoinebou12/Artemis-Switch

★ 26 · 2 forks · Repository created 2026-08-08

GitHub statistics recorded 2026-10-20.

A stream can report a healthy bitrate and still feel late. Artemis Switch is my Moonlight-Switch fork for Nintendo Switch, focused on the path between receiving a frame and presenting it. The useful question is not just “how fast is the decoder?” but “where did this frame wait?”

item.title: Porting sm64coopdx to Switch and New 3DS: keep the platform boundary small
item.description:
antoinebou12/sm64coopdx-switch-N3DS

★ 3 · 1 forks · Repository created 2026-08-19

GitHub statistics recorded 2026-10-20.

The interesting part of a console port is rarely a single compiler flag. sm64coopdx-switch-N3DS brings the Coop Deluxe engine to two very different handheld targets. The work lives at the platform boundary: graphics, input, audio, threading, and packaging.

This fork builds on the Coop Deluxe Team’s sm64coopdx, which continues djoslin0’s sm64ex-coop. The multiplayer engine and Lua ecosystem are upstream work; the console adapters are the focus here.

item.title: Handheld streaming and homebrew — Artemis-Switch, moonlight-N3DS, sm64coopdx-switch
item.description: Three repos I maintain on the side: Artemis-Switch[1] for Apollo/Sunshine streaming on Switch, moonlight-N3DS[2] for GameStream on New 3DS, and sm64coopdx-switch[3] as a Switch build of cooperative Super Mario 64. They share the same itch — run something interesting on hardware that was not designed for it — but the stack and constraints differ.
